title: Agent Evaluation Corpus
description: A versioned set of benchmark tasks for one service. Tasks name source operations, never tool names: a task naming a tool could describe one planner's output and would be unable to describe the other, which defeats the comparison the corpus exists to make.

source_digest.description: Specification revision the tasks were written against. A corpus describing other bytes cannot judge this service.

authoring_note.description: How the tasks were authored, so a reader can judge their independence from the surface they score.

stateAssertion.description: One deterministic claim about the service state a task should leave behind.

contains.description: Assert the value references this, rather than equals it. A service names things in more than one form, and an agent that sends the fuller one is right, so equality would fail a correct call.

oracle.description: One check applied to a completed run. `final_state` is the criterion the acceptance rules single out: success is judged by the state the service ends in, not by whether the trace resembled an expected one. `retrieval` exists because a read changes no state, so every other check is negative and an agent that does nothing satisfies them all.

referenceStep.description: One step of a solution the author asserts is correct. Not a scoring key: a run is judged by its oracles, so replaying these steps can still fail if the resulting state is wrong.

fixture.description: Starting service state, as collection to record identifier to record.

retrievalAssertion.description: One claim that a value was actually returned. Checked against the recorded response, never by a judge.

operation_id.description: Restrict the check to responses from this operation. Usually a mistake: a goal asks for an outcome, and pinning the operation asserts a route instead, so an agent that reaches the same outcome by a better route is marked wrong.

field.description: Dotted path into the response; null searches anywhere.

contains.description: Assert the value references this, rather than equals it. A service names things in more than one form, and an agent that sends the fuller one is right, so equality would fail a correct call.
